source: NCERT Class XII, Politics in India Since Independence, Ch. 2 (Era of One-Party Dominance).

sections.heading: 1. The First General Elections
points: India held its **first general elections in 1951–52** — a huge exercise of **universal adult franchise** in a poor, largely illiterate country.
The **Election Commission (under Sukumar Sen)** conducted it successfully — a landmark for democracy.
The **Congress won** a big majority.

sections.heading: 2. Congress Dominance
points: For the first three general elections (1952, 1957, 1962), the **Indian National Congress dominated** — a period of **one-party dominance**.
Reasons: the Congress's role in the **freedom struggle (legacy)**, its **broad social base and 'umbrella' character** (accommodating diverse groups/ideologies), and the weak, divided opposition.
This dominance was achieved through **democratic (free and fair) means** — unlike one-party systems elsewhere.

sections.heading: 3. The Congress as a Coalition
points: The Congress was itself a **broad coalition/'umbrella party'** — bringing together diverse interests, ideologies, castes and communities.
It practised **accommodation and tolerance of internal factions** (a 'system of managing conflicts').
This absorbed potential opposition within the party.

sections.heading: 4. The Opposition Parties
points: Despite Congress dominance, a **vibrant opposition existed** (kept democracy alive).
Opposition parties: **Socialist Party, Communist Party (CPI), Bharatiya Jana Sangh, Swatantra Party**.
Leaders: **Ram Manohar Lohia, Jayaprakash Narayan, Shyama Prasad Mukherjee, A.K. Gopalan, Minoo Masani**.
The opposition raised issues and provided alternatives, ensuring accountability.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: First general elections = 1951–52 (Sukumar Sen = first CEC).
Congress dominated the first three elections (1952, 1957, 1962).
Congress = 'umbrella party' / broad coalition (accommodation).
Opposition: Socialist, CPI, Jana Sangh, Swatantra.
One-party dominance achieved by democratic means.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India's **first general election was in 1951–52** (Sukumar Sen conducted it).
Congress dominance was through **free and fair (democratic) means** (not authoritarianism).
The Congress was a **broad 'umbrella' coalition** of diverse groups.
**Swatantra Party** and **Jana Sangh** were among the opposition parties.
